text:
olivia: Heads-up - merged Apricot LoRA into integration earlier and kicked off the on-board quickpack. Strange tokenization-ish failures on invoice parsing with rw-7b-int4.

matt: can you paste the failing sample? short is fine, we just need to triage whether it's token->quant or adapter-side.

olivia: sample below (sanitized):
```
PROMPT: "Extract items, qty, unit_price from invoice:"
RW-7B-INT4: "1) Widget A - qty 2 - $10\n2) service fee - $5\nNote: discount applied\n"
EXPECTED: "1) Widget A - qty 2 - $10"
```
extra lines only appear on int4. int8 and fp16 run locally looked clean when I spot-checked.

sanjay: did the fine-tune bundle ship a tokenizer override? sometimes adapter training adds special tokens and we accidentally use the base model tokenizer in inference.

olivia: the finetune bundle includes tokenizer.json but our eval CLI defaults to model repo tokenizer. I ran `rwi eval run --pack apricot-quickpack --model rw-7b-int4` (no override).

matt: quick experiment: try `--tokenizer-path /mnt/finetunes/apricot/tokenizer.json` and also `--force-gptq-config per_channel=true,symmetric=true`. if token alignment helps, it's adapter tokenizer. if GPTQ helps, it's quant.

ana: (from ana) also run a token-diff for the substring "service" against both tokenizers: `rwi util token-diff --a /mnt/finetunes/apricot/tokenizer.json --b /models/rw-7b/tokenizer.json` - that'll show id drift.

zhi: CI note: build 2026-03-17_0831 for apricot/lora succeeded; added smoke tests but not the invoice gating test yet.

olivia: ran both overrides. results:
- with adapter tokenizer: regression reduced but still occasionally produces the extra "service" line (20% of seeds).
- with GPTQ per_channel symmetric config: regression disappears in 95% of runs.

matt: that indicates quant configuration interacting with token logits near boundaries. int4 with default GPTQ likely used asymmetric quant which amplifies small logits into spurious tokens.

sanjay: follow-ups: 1) mark rw-7b-int4 as "experimental / NOT-RECOMMENDED" for Apricot in the onboard matrix until we pick a stable GPTQ config; 2) add deterministic gating test to apricot-quickpack that asserts no extra lines for the invoice sample across seeds 0/42/123; 3) add token-diff step to the onboarding CI to catch tokenizer id mismatches early.

ana: I'll open PRs: one for docs (onboarding matrix), one for the quickpack tests, and one for CI util to run token-diff.

olivia: filed issue AP-421 with eval logs + sample seeds. attaching `eval-logs/apricot-int4-seed42.log`. tagging @matt @sanjay @ana @zhi.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline: apricot-integration -> smoke passed, tests pending (invoice-gate test not yet merged). :gear:

matt: good catch. once gating test is in CI we should block merges if the int4 config regresses. for immediate mitigation, add a recommended GPTQ config to the model card for Apricot (`gptq: per_channel: true, symmetric: true, bits: 4`).

sanjay: also add a short note in the finetune bundle README about tokenizer provenance and include `rwi util tokenizer-check` in the quick start. small guardrails save hours.

olivia: thanks folks. i'll follow up with a short post in #product to notify QA and support about the int4 advisory. :thumbsup:
